title: T. Rex Body Temperature Was Similar to Our Own
paragraphs: Tyrannosaurus rex is one of the most famous dinosaurs of all time. Now, a new study suggests that the giant predator had a body temperature very similar to that of humans.
The study was published in the journal Science Advances in September 2026. It was carried out by researchers including Aradhna Tripati and Robert Eagle of the University of California, Los Angeles.

Measuring the body temperature of an animal that died millions of years ago is extremely difficult. As one scientist put it, researchers cannot simply use a thermometer. Instead, the team looked for chemical clues in fossilized T. rex teeth. Inside tooth enamel, atoms clump together in different patterns depending on an animal's body temperature. By studying these patterns, the researchers could estimate how warm the animal was.

Readings from three teeth showed that T. rex had an average body temperature of about 36 degrees Celsius. This is similar to modern elephants, and close to the normal human body temperature of 36 to 37 degrees Celsius.

In the past, scientists believed that dinosaurs were slow, cold-blooded animals. However, later research suggested that some dinosaurs were warm-blooded and could control their own body temperature. Most scientists now agree that T. rex was warm-blooded, but earlier methods, such as studying how its bones grew, had not produced a firm number.

According to Tripati, this temperature would have allowed T. rex to live across most of prehistoric North America, keeping a stable temperature in both cooler and hotter areas. The findings may also help scientists understand how much food T. rex needed to keep up its energy.

Interestingly, not everyone expected this result. Jasmina Wiemann, a paleobiologist at Johns Hopkins University who was not involved in the study, said that she had expected T. rex to be a few degrees warmer, like modern birds.
Scientists now hope to use the same method to study other dinosaurs. According to Eagle, there are many other species that could be studied in this way.
